convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load the X2MA custom indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh for CXMA class and TradeAlgorithms.mqh for trading functions). The smoothing methods include non-standard types (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) beyond built-in MT5 indicators.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required for calculation
derived_values.used_by: BarsCalculated check and X2MA indicator stability gate

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - chart period in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for trade signal timestamp

other_exits: Opposite signal triggers close of existing position when BuyPosClose/SellPosClose permissions are enabled

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Negative MM values = fixed lot size (e.g. -0.1 means 0.1 lots). Positive MM values = deposit fraction (share of deposit in deal). Controlled by TradeAlgorithms.mqh implementation.

custom_logic_notes: The X2MA indicator is a double-smoothed MA: first smoothing (MA_Method1/Length1/Phase1) applied to price, then second smoothing (MA_Method2/Length2/Phase2) applied to the result. Entry logic: if X2MA[1]<X2MA[2] (MA rising over 2 bars) AND X2MA[0]>X2MA[1] (still rising at signal bar), then buy signal. If X2MA[1]>X2MA[2] (MA falling) AND X2MA[0]<X2MA[1] (still falling), then sell signal. Signal is evaluated on new bar or on SignalBar=0 every tick. The Value array holds 3 consecutive X2MA buffer values starting at SignalBar offset. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose boolean inputs act as permission gates. GlobalVariableDel_ is called on deinit for cleanup. LoadHistory is called to ensure bar data availability for IsNewBar and SeriesInfoInteger.
python_conversion_notes: The X2MA custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python. It chains two smoothing operations: first pass applies MA_Method1 (supports SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA, JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) with Length1/Phase1 to the selected price type, then second pass applies MA_Method2 with Length2/Phase2 to the first result. The non-standard smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh have no direct Python library equivalents and must be ported individually. TradeAlgorithms.mqh encapsulates all order execution (open/close with MM logic, SL/TP, deviation handling) - this must be reimplemented or replaced with a broker API wrapper. The position sizing conditional logic (negative=lot, positive=deposit share) needs careful handling. Entry signal uses 3-bar lookback of the double-smoothed MA values to confirm trend direction consistency.
